Deep and Shallow Decarbonization in Supply Chains
with Alvaro Pedraza
Using global supplier-customer links matched to firm-level emissions and project-level data from voluntary carbon registries, we show that downstream climate pressure propagates upstream, eliciting both real and symbolic responses, but in systematically different ways across suppliers. PDF

Environmental Performance and Stock Market Valuations: Global Evidence on the Pricing of Polluters
Approximating a firm’s greenness with emission levels and intensities in a global sample of firms from 2006 to 2022, this paper analyzes whether differences in environmental performance are reflected in relative stock market valuations. PDF

The financial origins of regional inequality
with Sebastian Doerr
Journal of Money, Credit and Banking, accepted.
Using a quasi-natural experiment on bank branching deregulation, we show that removing financial restrictions disproportionately benefited urban relative to rural regions — primarily by boosting labor demand, employment, and wages in cities.

Understanding firm networks in global agricultural value chains
with Sunghum Lim and Daria Taglioni
Food Policy, Volume 127, August 2024, 102689.
Tracking roughly 17,500 agribusiness companies and over 150,000 supplier-customer connections, this paper examines the evolution of global value chains in the agrifood sector from 2014 to 2022. Large corporations have strengthened their network centrality through geographic diversification and concentrated supply strategies, with greater connectivity associated with higher resilience.

title: Anne Beck
text:
I am an Economist at the World Bank’s Development Economics Research Group. My research sits at the intersection of trade, sustainability, and finance. Drawing on micro data, I study how climate and trade policies reshape global value chains and local labor markets, and how the financial sector shapes real outcomes. Recent projects include the propagation of decarbonization strategies in global value chains, the employment and political effects of tariff changes, financial intermediation and spatial disparities, and the opportunities and challenges of a circular economy transition. I hold a Ph.D. in Economics from the University of Zurich, Switzerland.
